warnings.details: NOTIN EYE DROPS is not recommended for use in pregnant women unless considered necessary by the physician. Therefore, inform your doctor before using NOTIN EYE DROPS if you are pregnant, think you may be pregnant or planning to have a baby. Women of child-bearing potential must use a suitable contraceptive method to avoid pregnancy while undergoing therapy with NOTIN EYE DROPS.
NOTIN EYE DROPS can be used in breastfeeding women if prescribed by the doctor. Consult your doctor for advice.
Do not drive or operate any machines if you experience blurred vision after using NOTIN EYE DROPS. Wait, until your vision becomes clear.
Do not use NOTIN EYE DROPS if you are allergic to nepafenac or to other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines (such as ibuprofen, aspirin, piroxicam, ketoprofen, diclofenac).
NOTIN EYE DROPS is not recommended for use in patients who previously developed asthma while using any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Therefore, consult your doctor before application.

Others

NOTIN EYE DROPS is not recommended for use if you:

Had previously experienced any skin allergy or intense inflammation in your nose following the use of any pain relieving medicines

Before using NOTIN EYE DROPS, inform your doctor if you:

Bruise easily or have any bleeding problems
Have an eye infection or any other eye disorders
Have diabetes
Have rheumatoid arthritis (inflammation of joints)
Have had repeated eye surgery within a short period of time

Use in pediatrics:

NOTIN EYE DROPS is generally not recommended for use in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years). Therefore, consult your doctor before application.

Use in geriatrics:

NOTIN EYE DROPS should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years and above). Therefore, consult your doctor before application.

name: AUROSPORINE Ophthalmic Solution 5ml
introduction:
Introduction About AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION

AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION contains Cyclosporin which belongs to the group of medicines called Immunosuppressants.  It is used to manage severe dry eye syndrome (keratoconjunctivitis sicca) in children and in adolescents (aged between 4-18 years).

Dry Eye Syndrome (also known as keratoconjunctivitis sicca) is an allergic eye condition that affects the transparent layer in the front part of the eye and the thin membrane covering the front part of the eye. It is characterized by excessive eye dryness, redness, itching, inflammation and discomfort. Persons having dry eye syndrome do not produce sufficient tears to lubricate and nourish the eyes.

AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION is for ophthalmic use only. Wash your hands before and after application. Avoid touching the tip of the container with your mouth, nose or other parts of body to avoid contamination.

If you wear soft contact lenses, make sure to remove them before using AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION. Consult your doctor about the usage of contact lenses while undergoing management for dry eyes.

Before using AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION inform your doctor if you have any other eye conditions apart from dry eye syndrome such as eye infection or glaucoma. AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION is not recommended for use in patients having cancer in and around the eye areas. Consult your doctor before using AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.

The most common side effects of using AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION are eye pain, redness, irritation or discomfort, watery eyes and blurred vision. Consult your doctor if they trouble you.
uses: Manage severe dry eye syndrome
usesDetails:
Uses Of AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION
Manage severe dry eye syndrome
mechanismOfAction:
How AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION Works

AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION is an immunosuppressive agent. Following application on the eyes, it blocks the release of certain chemicals in the eye (such as T-cells, interleukins and cytokines) that causes eye inflammation, allergies and discomfort. As a result, it reduces inflammation and swelling on the eye and keeps your eyes lubricated by allowing your eye to produce tears.
usageDetails:
How to use AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION

Use AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION as advised by your physician. It is for ophthalmic use only. Wash your hands before application. Tilt your head slightly backwards and place the tip of the container close to your eyes.

Gently pull your lower eyelid and instil few drops of the medicine as directed by your physician. Close your eyes and gently press the inner corner of your eye for 2 minutes. Repeat the same for the other eye if required.

Do not touch the tip of the container with your eyes, eyelids or areas around your eyes or fingers, to avoid contamination. Avoid wearing contact lenses while undergoing therapy for dry eyes.

Your doctor will decide the correct dose and duration of therapy for you depending upon your age, body weight and disease condition. Do not stop using AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION unless your doctor tells you to stop.

Sensation of foreign body in the eye

AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION should be used with caution in breast-feeding women. Therefore, consult your doctor before using it.

AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION may temporarily blur your vision. Therefore, do not drive or handle any heavy tools or machines if you experience blurred vision after applying AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION.
Consumption of alcohol is not recommended during management with AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION.
Do not use AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION if you are allergic to cyclosporin.

Others

Have or ever had cancer in or around eyes
Have an eye infection

Before using AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION inform your doctor if you:

Had an eye infection (herpes viral infection) or suspect of having it
Have any other eye problems (such as glaucoma)

AUROSPORINE OPHTHALMIC SOLUTION is not recommended for use in children (aged below 4 years). Therefore, consult your doctor before using it.

Do not use NEPAZE OPHTHALMIC SUSPENSION if you are allergic to nepafenac or to other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicines (such as ibuprofen, aspirin, piroxicam, ketoprofen, diclofenac).

NEPAZE OPHTHALMIC SUSPENSION is not recommended for use in patients who previously developed asthma while using any non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. Therefore, consult your doctor before application.

Others

NEPAZE OPHTHALMIC SUSPENSION is not recommended for use if you:

Had previously experienced any skin allergy or intense inflammation in your nose following the use of any pain relieving medicines

Before using NEPAZE OPHTHALMIC SUSPENSION, inform your doctor if you:

Bruise easily or have any bleeding problems
Have an eye infection or any other eye disorders
Have diabetes
Have rheumatoid arthritis (inflammation of joints)
Have had repeated eye surgery within a short period of time

Use in pediatrics:

NEPAZE OPHTHALMIC SUSPENSION is generally not recommended for use in children and adolescents (aged below 18 years). Therefore, consult your doctor before application.

Use in geriatrics:

NEPAZE OPHTHALMIC SUSPENSION should be used with caution in elderly patients (aged 65 years and above). Therefore, consult your doctor before application.

interactions:
Interactions

A. Drug-Drug interactions:

Before using NEPAZE OPHTHALMIC SUSPENSION, inform your doctor if you are taking any of the following medicines such as:

Other eye drops for the management of glaucoma (Ex. timolol)
Medicines used to reduce blood clotting (Ex. warfarin)
Other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs to reduce pain (Ex. aspirin, ibuprofen, ketoprofen, piroxicam, diclofenac)
Topical steroids on the eye (Ex. hydrocortisone)

Overdosage:

If you or anyone else accidentally used more NEPAZE OPHTHALMIC SUSPENSION, rinse your eye with warm water. If still irritation persists, consult your doctor.
